selftest_literals.value:
kengaku hermetic evidence-replay grader — the operability gate (round 10;
round-11 tree added in round 11).

Replays the committed probe evidence OFFLINE (no endpoint, no network) and
exits with a verdict a stranger can run:

    python3 grader.py            # grade the committed evidence
    python3 grader.py --selftest # corrupt temp copies; all must be caught

Exit codes (kagi drift-pins convention):
    0  every recomputed value matches the stored one
    1  at least one mismatch; each printed as `MISMATCH <check-id>: ...`
    2  missing/unreadable input, or unparseable evidence

What it verifies, layer by layer:
  PIN     evidence bytes == the hashes recorded when they landed (pins are
          checked only when the DEFAULT in-repo paths are graded; overridden
          paths are by definition mutated copies).
  META    every meta record regenerates exactly from its seed through the
          ported gen_problem (r8: 700+pid*13, pids 1-10; r9: 2000+pid*29,
          pids 101-108; r11: 3000+pid*41, pids 201-264), and stored
          truth/tail_touched re-derive from init+ops through sim_apply.
  REPLAY  every graded record's stored got/want/ok/nwrong equals a fresh
          re-parse of its stored `raw` (extract_json_block ported verbatim
          from horizon.py) re-graded against the meta-derived truth;
          B-records also re-derive corrupt_from/outcome/healed; C-records
          re-run grade_c / valid_latin.
  SUMMARY every stored aggregate re-derives from the replayed records:
          r8 run.log `=== SUMMARY ===` (11 cells) + job/record counts;
          r9 replication.md observed table (passes + mean final nwrong),
          record counts, sign tests, onset ladder, failure classes, ack
          compliance, finish-reason claim, cross-round table, prediction
          scoring table vs predictions-r9.md, prediction-hash chain and
          the ordering proof (hash time <= first request_ts);
          r11 analysis_r11.md (observed table, census sentence, paired
          diff/t/CI, exact sign + McNemar, mechanical verdict rule, Brier,
          point-prediction scoring), run.log SUMMARY (2 cells), the
          preregistration-bundle sha256 chain and the ordering proof
          (stats: NR betai t-CDF + math.comb exacts, stdlib only).
  ERRATA  adjudicated corrections are pinned in ERRATA below: a check whose
          stored value was ruled defective in a later round passes iff the
          recomputation equals the ADJUDICATED value and the stored text
          still shows the original (the erratum chain stays visible).

gen_problem regeneration) and the graders of corpus/evidence/round8-horizon/
horizon.py (extract_json_block / sim_apply / grade_state / grade_c) into a
committed gate. Stdlib only. Deterministic: never orders results by set
iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent).

Re-derive every stored round-11 number from committed bytes.

    `pids`/`seed_fn` default to the preregistered n=64 (pids 201-264,

selftest_literals.value:
Interval-calibrated verdicts for the lane's blind attribution instrument
(kengaku round 25, claim C1 — plans/round-25-claims.md:21-66).

Re-derives OFFLINE, from committed receipt bytes only, how accurate
plans/attrib_probe.py's blind leg attribution is, as exact intervals, and
re-verdicts every stored point verdict. Receipts are read, never written; no
journal, endpoint or network is touched.

Population P1 (claims:28-33): corpus/evidence/attrib-r2[123]-*.log under
--root. Per file the scored block is the LAST "## GT + scoring at close" block
(the receipts' own AUTHORITATIVE SCORING SECTION rule,
attrib-r21-impl-ds-trials.log:316); a file without one is trial-only and
reports accuracy 0/0 -> UNTESTED. Authoritative blocks whose trial tables are
identical (same trial ids, predictions, GT, chains) are one sample: the
earliest-scored block is kept and every later one is named as its duplicate
and not counted. When --root has no corpus/evidence directory, every *.log
directly under it is read instead (fixture trees).

Estimates per kept block: overall accuracy; per-leg recall (GT == leg);
per-leg specificity, one-vs-rest (GT != leg and prediction != leg); every
stored TARGET / STREAM TARGET clause; and per leg the predicted share q with
its Rogan-Gladen true-share bound. Legs = the keys of the receipt's blind
`scores={...}` lines plus every leg named in the table.

Frozen rule (claims:35-40): two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson; PASS iff lower >=
bar, FAIL iff upper < bar, INDETERMINATE otherwise, UNTESTED iff n == 0; bar =
the line's own stated bar (0.80). The receipts' min-n (20 overall, 10 per
target) belongs to the stored point rule: it is re-applied when stored verdicts
are re-derived and reported in --json, never used by the interval rule. Wilson
95% is a sensitivity column, never a verdict. Leg-share bound: min/max of
(q + sp - 1) / (se + sp - 1) over se in [se_L, 1], sp in [sp_L, 1] (CP lower
bounds of recall / specificity), clipped to [0, 1]. The function is monotone in
each coordinate wherever se + sp > 1, so the four corners give the extremes;
when se_L + sp_L - 1 <= 0 the box reaches the pole se + sp = 1 and the bound is
the vacuous [0, 1]. Same plug-in sensitivity/specificity correction as the
judge-bias accounting of S011 (corpus/SOURCES.md:33).

Stored-line re-derivation covers every block, superseded ones included: each
row's `correct` cell, `GT counts`, `ACCURACY`, `TARGET`, `BODY`, `STREAM TARGET`
and the `score_summary` record are recomputed from the block's own rows with
attrib_probe.py cmd_score's arithmetic (plans/attrib_probe.py:965-1106).

Usage:  python3 plans/attrib_calibration.py [--root DIR] [--summary|--json] [--selftest]
Exit:   0 ran and every stored line re-derives from its own rows;
        1 parse/recompute inconsistency or selftest failure;
        2 usage (bad --root, no receipts). INDETERMINATE is a finding, not an error.

Numerics: CP bounds are Beta quantiles — lower = Beta(k, n-k+1) at alpha/2,
upper = Beta(k+1, n-k) at 1-alpha/2 — found by bisection on grader.py's
continued-fraction `betai` (grader.py:879-925, Numerical Recipes 6.4), loaded
from this checkout without running grader's CLI and without writing bytecode.
Sources: Clopper & Pearson 1934, Biometrika 26(4):404-413,
doi:10.1093/biomet/26.4.404; SciPy 1.18.0 BinomTestResult.proportion_ci
("'exact' : Use the Clopper-Pearson exact method") and its binomtest(k=7, n=50)
example, used as a selftest anchor; Wilson 1927, JASA 22(158):209-212; Rogan &
Gladen 1978, Am J Epidemiol 107(1):71-76.

selftest_literals.value:
Source-adoption gate for kengaku's corpus registry.

Round 29 attempt 2 (2026-10-25). The fleet census (`scripts/sources-census.sh`)
validates a registry that already exists; nothing in the lane checked a row set
*before* it was appended. This gate does that check, so an adoption round cannot
append a colliding id, a mangled cell, or a `used-by` pointing at an entry that
was never admitted.

Capabilities (each separately exercised by `--selftest`):
  1. id-collision detection against the live registry, using the census parser's
     own 0-3-leading-space row anchor -- a column-zero-only pattern false-greens
     an indented collision (scratch `  | S002 |` fixture, SKILL/CORPUS note);
  2. staged-row schema check: exactly 11 cells, no literal or escaped `|` inside
     a cell, a valid `status`, and a valid `recheck` cell;
  3. append-block construction that normalizes a prose `recheck` cell to the
     frozen access date (reporting the stripped prose separately) and rewrites
     `used-by` to exactly the admitted entries citing the row;
  4. refusal with a non-zero exit for a missing requested id, an escaped pipe, a
     duplicate staged id, or a nonempty collision set;
  5. quote validation (`--quote-file`/`--artifact`): every quoted span in a supplied
     row's anchor cell is measured against the contract's <=25-word cap and located
     as a byte substring of the named artifact, with its own exit codes;
  6. capture-to-citation binding (`--url-map`): the artifact that located a quote must be
     mapped to the URL that row's `source` cell cites, so a capture of some other document
     cannot satisfy a row it happens to share a sentence with.

Scope: registry row mechanics and quote presence only. Source truth, tier judgement
and the census itself stay where they are (CORPUS.md contract v1; census is
fleet-owned).

Mined from the round-39 closure item F39CritQ30 (`corpus/QUALITY.md` Q30): the order class
"a frozen probe must not run before its receipt is committed" is recorded as *closed by a gate*,
and `plans/order_check.py` is that gate — but nothing in the lane invoked it. Round 39's ordering
held because the seat happened to commit the receipt second, not because a command checked. A gate
nothing calls is a claim, not a gate.

This is the caller. Given `--lane . --round N` it

  1. reads `plans/round-N-claims.md` (the round's frozen claims);
  2. resolves the receipt(s) the claims name (three rules, below);
  3. runs `plans/order_check.py --lane <lane> --claims ... --receipt ...` once per receipt;
  4. runs the fleet sources census in `validate` mode against the lane's `corpus/SOURCES.md`;
  5. exits 0 only when every leg passes.

Exit: 0 every leg passed · 1 a leg FAILED (order broken, or the census reported an E-code)
· 2 setup (a leg could not be evaluated: no claims file, no order tool, no census script, an
unreadable receipt, bad arguments). A leg that cannot be evaluated is never a pass.

Receipt resolution. The claims file names its own probe; the receipt is that probe's recorded run.
The lane has written the name three ways, so all three are read, deduplicated in this order:

  (a) an explicit mention on one line, `Receipt: `corpus/evidence/round37/...-probe.txt``
      (rounds 36 and 37 write it this way);
  (b) a backticked `corpus/evidence/roundN/...-probe.txt` path for this round
      (round 37's C2 surface paragraph);
  (c) derived from a `plans/<stem>_probe.py` the claims name, as
      `corpus/evidence/roundN/<stem with _ -> ->.txt` (rounds 38-40 name only the probe script,
      e.g. `plans/db_wal_probe.py` -> `corpus/evidence/round40/db-wal-probe.txt`).

A candidate that is neither a file in the lane nor committed in HEAD is reported as
`note=skipped-unreadable-receipt` and dropped; if no candidate survives, the round has no receipt
to gate and the run is a setup error (2), never a silent pass.

Self-test (`--selftest`, needs `--lane` for the tool and registry bytes): five two-commit fixture
repos in a temp dir, each differing only in where the receipt and one `P10` line sit — excused
`P10` detail -> 0, executed `P10` detail -> 1, receipt committed first -> 1, receipt on disk but
never committed -> 2, claims naming no receipt -> 2.

Read-only: the only git commands are the ones `plans/order_check.py` itself issues, plus one
`rev-parse` and `cat-file -e` here; the census script reads `corpus/SOURCES.md` and prints TSV.
Nothing is written, no network is touched, no probe, gate or counter is imported or executed.
`--selftest` writes only inside its own temp dir.

Limits named:
  * The census leg uses `--file <lane>/corpus/SOURCES.md`, not `--root <fleet> <lane-id>`. Both
    modes resolve E11 against the lane root and print the same findings; they differ only in the
    lane label of the TSV (`file` instead of `kengaku`), so `--file` needs no fleet roster and
    works unchanged on a clone. Measured on the live lane, 2026-10-26: identical 15 W04 + 2 E11.
    The script is found from `--census`, else `$SHOKUNIN_ROOT` (the census's own root contract),
    else the lane's parents; a clone that has neither is a setup error, never a skipped leg.
  * Census W-codes are warnings by the census contract ("0 clean or warnings") and do not fail the
    leg; their count is printed so a warning storm stays visible.
  * The census leg validates the work tree; the order leg reads commits only. Run this on a clean
    clone of the tip for a measurement that does not mix the two — an uncommitted registry row is
    invisible to the clone and visible (as E11/E12) to the work tree.
  * `--lane` must be the git work-tree top: `order_check.py` resolves its `--claims`/`--receipt`
    against the work-tree root, so a subdirectory lane would silently mean different paths.
  * It gates one round, not the round series: a round whose claims file was never committed is a
    setup error (2), and this tool does not scan earlier rounds.

scratch_guard.py -- sentinel-bound guard for a hyaku shared scratch root.

Round-41 closure R2 (defect D1): a wave-1 seat ran ``rm -rf`` on the shared round root and
destroyed other seats' work. The L1 already greps the sentinel before each measurement
(``.ufo/waves/round-42/integrate/measure.sh:9``); this tool gives every seat the same two
operations as one stdlib command, so nothing in the envelope needs shell ``rm``.

Commands
--------
``check <root> [--round N] [--json]``
    Exit 0 iff ``<root>/.ROUND-ROOT-SENTINEL`` exists and its content names the round
    (``kengaku r<NN> round root``, the round-42 wording at
    ``/fast/scratch/hyaku/kengaku-r42/.ROUND-ROOT-SENTINEL``). When ``--round N`` is given
    the named round must equal N. Every direct subdirectory (a seat; the L1 included) is
    printed with its apparent size; symlinked seats are marked and never walked.
    Exit 1 when the sentinel is missing, unparseable, or names another round; exit 2 when
    the root is not a directory or the sentinel cannot be read (cannot evaluate).
    Read-only: nothing under <root> is created, touched or written.

``safe-rm <root> <seat> <path> [--dry-run]``
    Delete ``<path>`` only when it resolves inside ``<root>/<seat>``; otherwise exit 2 and
    delete nothing. Refused, always:

    * the root itself, and any ancestor of it (``target-is-root``);
    * ``<root>/.ROUND-ROOT-SENTINEL`` (``target-is-sentinel``);
    * another seat's directory or anything under it
      (``target-resolves-outside-seat`` / ``target-outside-seat``);
    * any path containing a ``..`` component, before resolution (``target-dotdot``);
    * a target that is, or is reached through, a symlink resolving outside the seat
      (``target-resolves-outside-seat``) -- ``rm -rf`` would follow the parent link while
      walking, so the resolved path, not the literal one, decides;
    * ``<root>/<seat>`` that is itself a symlink (``seat-is-symlink``): a link named after
      seat A must never delete seat B's bytes;
    * a seat name that is not one path component (``seat-invalid``) and a root whose
      sentinel is absent or unreadable (``root-untrusted`` / ``root-not-a-directory``).

    Allowed: any path at or below ``<root>/<seat>``, including the seat directory itself (a
    seat's cleanup trap deletes its own ``$S``). A relative ``<path>`` is relative to
    ``<root>/<seat>`` -- never to the caller's cwd -- so ``cd`` cannot move the anchor.
    A missing target prints ``ABSENT`` and exits 0 (traps re-run); a refused delete exits 2.

``--selftest``
    Builds a throwaway root under ``TMPDIR`` with seats, a symlinked seat, an outside tree
    and a sentinel, then drives every refusal and every allow through the same dispatch as
    the CLI. Each refusal case also proves it is able to fail: the refused target still
    exists, is writable, and the same naive operation succeeds on a twin at a legal path.
    Exit 0 iff every case passes; prints ``SELFTEST ok=<k>/<n>``.

Exit codes: ``0`` ok / deleted / absent; ``1`` check red (sentinel missing, unparseable,
round mismatch) or a failing selftest case; ``2`` usage, cannot evaluate, or a refused
delete. Stdlib only; no subprocess, no network, no shell.
kengaku r42 round root; L1 selftest; seats delete only $S/<SeatName>

selftest_literals.value:
Require every conditional refusal in a lesson's Gate section to be resolved.

A Gate row that refuses a candidate and states a flip condition — "Flip: ...",
"... flips when ...", "if ... admit ..." — is an obligation on a later round,
because the condition can fire at landing. Round 42 is the measured instance:
its `Dockerfile` reject says "if the entry keeps the `WORKDIR /app` sentence
..., admit `Dockerfile` as a tier-B mechanism row", the landed entry kept the
sentence and made it load-bearing, no `S###` row was ever opened, and nobody
recorded that the flip had fired (`.ufo/waves/round-42/falsify/` D3; the
round's own Gate prose at `corpus/lessons/round-42.md:44`).

The checker reads one lesson file (one `--lesson` argument), takes the `## Gate`
section, keeps the refusals that carry a flip condition, and requires each to
be resolved by a LATER line of the same lesson:

    Flip check (round N): <item> — fired|not fired — <evidence>

Rules, in the order they are applied:

1. Section. `## Gate` is matched as a level-2 heading and ends at the next
   level-1 or level-2 heading (or EOF). No such section is a setup error.
2. Refusals. A table row (a `|`-delimited line in the section, header and
   `---` separator skipped) is a refusal when its verdict cell — the second
   cell — matches REJECT, REJECTED, REFUSE or REFUSED case-insensitively.
   A bullet (`- ...` / `* ...`) is a refusal when it carries the same words.
   A row whose verdict says "Admitted" is not a refusal and is not counted
   even though admitted rows usually carry a flip sentence too; a row that is
   only "Captured, not a row" is not an explicit REJECT and is likewise not
   counted. That exclusion is deliberate and is visible in `refused_rows=`.
3. Flips. A refusal carries its flip in its own text (`flip:`, `flips when`,
   `if ... admit` — the three shapes the lessons use) or in a companion line of
   the same section that names the refused candidate: the round-30 shape, where
   the table's rejects are followed by a bullet list "Flip conditions (one per
   rejected candidate)". A companion line that names no refused candidate is
   not attached, and a refusal with no flip at all is not an obligation.
4. Resolution. A line matching `Flip check (round N): <item> — <state> —
   <evidence>` resolves a row when (a) it sits after the row's flip statement,
   (b) `<item>` equals the row's item or is that item plus a qualifier
   (`Dockerfile @ 2fd12b88`), (c) `<state>` is `fired` or `not fired`,
   (d) `<evidence>` has at least two words and is not a placeholder
   (`none`, `n/a`, `todo`, `tbd`, `-`, ...), and (e) N is not smaller than the
   round in the lesson's file name. `--` is accepted as a separator when the
   em dash is not used. A line that starts `Flip check (round` but breaks the
   shape is reported as malformed and resolves nothing. When several lines
   name the same item, the last one decides: an appended correction
   supersedes the line it corrects, and a later malformed or thin-evidence
   line leaves the obligation unresolved.

5. Citation leg (round 44). A `not fired` resolution that names a file is
   checked against the entry the lesson's Gate concerns: the `.md` files the
   Gate section names resolve under the lesson repo's `corpus/knowledge/`
   (plus any `--entry` path), and when one of them carries a
   `<file>:<line>` citation of a file the `not fired` line names, the line is
   red (`FLIP-CITE ... verdict=RED`). Round 43 is the measured instance: its
   `task.toml` reject is recorded `not fired` while the landed entry cites
   `task.toml:22` twice as the only ceiling on the graded call
   (`corpus/knowledge/tb2-feal-differential-cryptanalysis-grader.md:122`,
   `:300`; disagreement `corpus/lessons/round-43-verifier-spotcheck.md:129-141`).
   The leg only reads a `not fired` line that the checker accepts as the
   resolution; a `fired` line is never tested, and a Gate whose entries are
   absent leaves the leg inactive (`FLIP-CITE entries=-`).

Exit: 0 every conditional refusal is resolved and no `not fired` resolution
names a file an entry cites; 1 either defect is present (the `FLIPS` and
`FLIP-CITE` lines carry the counts); 2 setup/usage (unreadable lesson, no
`## Gate` section, argparse).

`--selftest` builds fixtures in a temporary directory and runs this script on
them as a subprocess, so both the parser and the CLI are exercised: each case
is expected red (exit 1) or green (exit 0) and the run prints one line per
case plus `SELFTEST ok=<k>/<n>`.

Limits, named: the section split is heading-based, so a lesson that puts its
Gate table under `### Gate` is a setup error rather than a guess; a cell
containing a literal `|` is read as extra cells (the verdict is still cell 2,
the rest only widen the scanned text); a companion flip line attaches to
every refused candidate it names (a bullet naming two ids obliges both) and
its item is the bullet's first code span, so a bullet whose candidate is
described only in prose attaches only when the prose matches the cell
verbatim after markdown stripping; the tool checks that a flip was
*recorded*, never that the recorded consequence was the right one, so a
`fired` line whose evidence contradicts its own landing passes; it reads the
working tree only and has no opinion about history, so a resolution line that
was committed and later deleted is invisible; one obligation per row is
assumed, so a row carrying two independent flip conditions is resolved by one
line naming it; and the citation leg is a name match, not a reading: it sees
`<file>:<line>` where the file name and the line stand together, so an entry
that names the file in one cell and the line in the next (`| cmd | task.toml |
:22 |`) is not seen, an extension-less name outside its small literal set is
not seen, a `<file>:<range>` inside a longer citation list is seen once for
the whole entry, a cited *directory* is not seen, and an entry it cannot
resolve under `corpus/knowledge/` is reported `missing` rather than judged.
SELFTEST case=%s expect=%s got=%s total=%s unresolved=%s not_fired=%s cite_red=%s rc=%d %s

Round-63 gate checks: provenance trio and grader-class decision-table depth.

Frozen by ``plans/round-63-claims.md`` (base tip c78749a5) — R63-C2 and the
section "Frontier step — provenance-trio gate". The predicates are fixed
there; this instrument only measures them, never re-defines them.

Subcommands
-----------

``trio <file>``
    Exit 0 iff lines matching ``^(source|verified-at|recheck):`` appear, in
    that order, within the first 12 lines and before the first line starting
    with ``## ``. Prints ``TRIO pass <file>`` or
    ``TRIO fail missing=<comma list> file=<file>``. Exit 1 on fail, 2 on usage.

``depth --skill <SKILL.md> --receipt <class-survey.txt> [--root <lane root>]``
    Locates the section heading line exactly
    ``## Decision table — grader class → offline replay recipe`` (em dash and
    arrow as written; missing section means 0 rows and fail). Table rows are
    lines in that section starting with ``|``; the first cell, stripped of
    spaces and backticks, is the class name; the header row and separator rows
    are ignored; expected columns are
    class | count | executed | replay recipe | receipt pointer (5 cells).
    The receipt's ``^CLASS (\S+) count=(\d+)`` names must equal the table's
    class-name set (16 names) and each row's count must equal the receipt's
    count. Every backticked token in the section containing ``/`` and ending
    in .py .md .json .txt .sh .lst .yml or ``/`` is a repo-relative path; it
    resolves iff it is relative, carries no ``..`` segment, and its lexically
    normalized ``root/token`` stays inside ``root`` (r64-C2: an absolute,
    ``..``-bearing or escaping token is a finding, never a resolution);
    share = resolved / total must be >= 0.90 with total > 0, and each row's
    receipt-pointer cell must hold at least one such token and at least one
    of them must resolve. Prints::

        ROWS n=<n> class_match=<True|False> count_mismatch=<k> paths total=<T> resolved=<R> share=<x.xx>
        [DETAIL ...]                       (only on fail)
        PREDICATE R63-C2 pass|fail         (always the last line)

    Exit 0 on pass, 1 on fail, 2 on usage.

``--selftest --work <dir>`` (alias ``selftest --work <dir>``)
    Builds, inside ``mkdtemp(dir=work)``, four fixtures — GOOD (16 rows
    matching a 16-CLASS fixture receipt, all paths resolving: must pass),
    BAD-COUNT (one count cell wrong: must fail), NO-SECTION (must fail) and
    BAD-ESCAPE (one row's receipt pointer is an absolute out-of-root path,
    plus one ``..`` token: must fail with ``DETAIL escape=``) — and exits 0
    iff all four behave. Fixtures are removed afterwards.

Ambiguity resolutions (the frozen rule is unchanged; see the seat report)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
* duplicate backticked paths are counted once (set semantics), so a repeated
  broken pointer is not double-priced;
* a row's pointer cell passes when it holds at least one path token and at
  least one of its tokens resolves; the section-wide share still prices the
  rest;
* a trio key appearing out of canonical order counts as not established and
  is therefore listed in ``missing=``;
* trailing whitespace on the decision-table heading is tolerated; leading
  whitespace, case and the em dash / arrow glyphs are compared exactly;
* the markdown header row is the row immediately above a separator row,
  whatever its wording (a first cell literally reading ``class`` is also
  ignored), because the frozen rule says to ignore the header row without
  fixing its text;
* a backticked token carrying a URL scheme (``scheme://``) is not a
  repo-relative path and is excluded from path accounting, so a citation of
  PEP 503 cannot depress the resolution share;
* tokens carrying a line suffix (``path.txt:11``) do not end in a counted
  suffix and are therefore not path tokens — the frozen definition is
  syntactic and is applied as written;
* an unreadable ``--skill`` / ``--receipt`` / argv file is a setup error
  (exit 2), never a vacuous pass;
* (2026-11-03, r64-C2) path tokens are confined to the root: an absolute
  token, a token carrying a ``..`` segment, or a token whose normalized
  ``root/token`` leaves the root is not resolved; the depth command reports
  the set as ``DETAIL escape=<tokens>`` and fails when it is nonempty, even
  when the >= 0.90 share clause alone would pass.

Round-64 provenance-trio sweep (R64-C3 freshness instrument).

Walks ``corpus/knowledge/*.md`` and classifies every entry:

* ``TRIO-OPEN`` -- the provenance trio (``source:``, ``verified-at:``,
  ``recheck:``) is established in canonical order inside the first 12 lines
  and before the first ``## `` heading.  This is EXACTLY the round-63 gate's
  rule: the function ``trio_missing`` is IMPORTED from
  ``plans/round63_gate_checks.py`` (``rule=import``), never re-implemented
  here, so the sweep cannot drift from the gate it mirrors.
* ``TRIO-ADDENDUM`` -- the opening predates the rule, and the file carries an
  append-only dated ``## Freshness addendum (round 64)`` block holding
  ``verified-at: 2026-11-03`` and a ``recheck:`` line with a non-empty
  command.
* ``TRIO-RED`` -- neither.

CLI
---
``--sweep --lane <L> [--frozen-list <path>]``
    Prints one ``SWEEP files=<n> trio_open=<a> addendum=<b> red=<c>`` line,
    then one line per non-OPEN entry (``ADDENDUM <path>`` / ``RED <path>``),
    then ``PREDICATE R64-C3 pass|fail``.  Paths are lane-relative POSIX.
    Exit 0 on pass, 1 on fail, 2 on setup.

``--selftest --work <dir>``
    Builds RED / ADDENDUM / OPEN fixtures under ``mkdtemp(dir=work)``,
    classifies each, and additionally exercises the sweep pipeline on a
    three-file fixture lane before and after a repair; exits 0 iff every
    case behaves as named.

SETUP cross-check (frozen list)
-------------------------------
``--sweep`` cross-checks its red set against the frozen base list
``corpus/evidence/round64/trio-red-at-base.txt`` (lane-local copy when
present, else the committed path in the lane repo; ``--frozen-list``
overrides).  While red entries are observed, the red set must equal the
frozen list entry-for-entry; any mismatch prints
``SETUP frozen-list-mismatch`` on stdout and exits 2 without a PREDICATE
line.  Once ``red=0`` there is no red set to compare: the cross-check is
then vacuous and the predicate is printed.  The frozen list is the BASE
population -- a repaired tip is expected to fall below it -- and this
resolution is what lets both the frozen red-before command and the frozen
counting command run with no extra flags.  On that ``red=0`` path every
frozen entry must still exist as a file in the lane: a deleted or renamed
entry is not a repair, so it prints ``SETUP frozen-entry-missing`` and exits
2 (an empty knowledge dir can therefore never pass).

Ambiguity resolutions (the frozen rule is unchanged; see the seat report)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
* ``TRIO-OPEN`` wins over an addendum: an entry whose opening already
  satisfies the gate counts OPEN and is not listed as non-OPEN;
* the addendum heading is compared with trailing whitespace tolerated (the
  gate's own heading comparison) and is exactly
  ``## Freshness addendum (round 64)``; a block runs to the next ``## ``
  heading or EOF, and any occurrence that carries both required lines
  classifies the entry ADDENDUM;
* inside the block ``verified-at:`` must carry the date token
  ``2026-11-03`` (bounded by whitespace/end of line, so trailing prose is
  tolerated but another date is not) and ``recheck:`` must carry a
  non-empty command; the ``ADDENDUM`` classification does not price the
  command's own exit status -- the closure re-runs it (frozen kill rule);
* a ``RED`` file that carries the heading but an incomplete block emits a
  ``NOTE addendum-incomplete`` diagnostic on stderr naming the missing
  lines; stdout stays exactly the frozen shape;
* an unreadable lane, knowledge dir or frozen list is a setup error
  (exit 2), never a vacuous pass.

log_appendonly.py — a committed log line is never rewritten (round 46).

Mined mistake (round-45 closure D1, `corpus/lessons/round-45-verifier-spotcheck.md` §1/§5 item 3): the closure's
`git diff -U0 fbad1c5 3d9ea54 -- LOG.md` shows two rewritten lines (`@@ -1374` heading and `@@ -1388` "A/B runs
byte-equal"). The per-commit walk attributes those deletions to `f660ae0`, the earlier commit in that range; it
also finds two different lines rewritten by `3d9ea54` itself (the `@@ -1407`–`@@ -1408` held-out tally). The lane's
own LOG.md recorded an earlier in-place rewrite (`LOG.md:9` cites `git diff 85b22e3 f147a27 -- LOG.md`, one
`-`/`+` pair). The stated rule — append a correction, never rewrite — had been enforced only by human diff review.

What is checked. For every commit reachable from HEAD that touches the log file, the commit's diff against its
first parent (merge commits compared to their mainline parent) is parsed hunk by hunk; every `-` line is a deletion
of a line that existed in the log before this commit, so it was committed earlier. A commit whose diff has only
`+` lines is a pure append and is fine. Line moves, whitespace-only edits and reorderings count: append-only means
never rewrite, so a moved line is still a rewritten line.

Output (oldest commit first), one line per offending commit and, under `--show-lines`, one line per deleted line:

    VIOLATION <sha12> <date> deleted=<n> at=<old-line[,old-line...]> first="<deleted text, <=72 chars>"
    DEL <sha12> :<old-line> -<deleted text, <=100 chars>
    LOG-APPENDONLY commits=<n> violations=<k>

`commits` counts the commits walked (log-touching commits in the bound range), `violations` the commits with at
least one deletion. Exit 0 iff `violations == 0`; 1 when it is > 0; 2 on a usage/setup error (no git, not a repo,
`--since` not an ancestor of HEAD).

Walk. `git log --full-history` — the same commits as plain `git log --format=%H -- LOG.md` plus every merge that
touches the file, which history simplification drops (at the round-46 base: 77 vs 76; the extra is the PR merge
`323b3921`, whose first-parent diff is 7 pure additions). `--verbose` prints that reconciliation on a `WALK` line.
Each commit is diffed against its first parent, so a merge's own conflict-resolution edit cannot hide.

`--since <rev>` binds the walk from a revision forward: only commits in `git log <rev>..HEAD` are inspected, so a
history already known to be clean before `<rev>` is not re-litigated. `<rev>` itself is not inspected (it is the
boundary, not an event); pass its parent to include it.

Read-only: no file in the repository is written, no index lock is taken (`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`), no commit or ref is
created. Diffs are read as text (`-a`) with no textconv and no rename detection, so a rewrite cannot hide behind a
binary guess, a rename or a filter. Subprocesses inherit `TMPDIR`; `--selftest` builds its fixture repos under a
`tempfile.mkdtemp()` honouring `TMPDIR`. Stdlib only.

Limits named: a commit that is not reachable from HEAD (an abandoned side branch) is not inspected; a log file that
did not exist in a commit's first parent has nothing to delete; `--since` trusts the caller that the earlier range
was clean.

Usage: python3 plans/log_appendonly.py [--lane DIR] [--path LOG.md] [--since REV] [--show-lines] [--verbose]

R84-C2 admission-bar counter for corpus/knowledge/tb2-code-from-image-offline.md.

Measured subject (one entry, one lesson):
  entry   corpus/knowledge/tb2-code-from-image-offline.md
  lesson  corpus/lessons/round-84.md          (Gate section is the successor admission)

Reads the entry (and the lesson) at the measured revision: `git show REV:path`
when --rev is present, the lane working tree when it is absent. Q13 is always
evaluated at a commit, because a Gate admission only exists once committed.

Rules as implemented (each is a line-level predicate on the entry bytes):

Q1  header contract. The first three lines must start, at column 0, with
    "source:", "verified-at:" and "recheck:" in that order. The recheck body
    (line 3 after "recheck:") must carry BOTH
      (a) a marker: an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date that is a real calendar date, or a
          cadence token (see CADENCE_RE: daily/weekly/bi-weekly/fortnightly/
          monthly/quarterly/semi-annual/annual/yearly/per-release/every <n> d|day|
          days|w|week|weeks|mo|month|months|h|hour|hours), and
      (b) a named re-check action: a command token (COMMAND_RE: python3, bash,
          npx, uv, make, git, jq, rg, go, cargo, npm, node, perl, ruby, curl,
          wget, bwrap, bubblewrap, or a plans/… .py / scripts/… .sh path), or the
          words re-verify/re-run (REVERB_RE) followed by a concrete action token
          (ACTION_TARGET_RE: a backticked span, a path-like token, a file with a
          .py/.sh/.json/.md/.txt/.yaml extension, or a command name).
    q1=1 if any component is missing; detail names the failures.

Q21 pin continuity. Every 40-hex token on the source line (PIN40_RE, with
    non-hex boundaries so a 64-hex digest cannot donate a 40-hex prefix) must be
    answered on the recheck line by either the same 40-hex value, or the words
    pin/re-pin (PIN_VERB_RE) together with a cadence token (CADENCE_RE, an ISO
    date is not a cadence here). q21=1 otherwise; q21=0 when the source line
    carries no 40-hex token (the rule is vacuous, not silently passed).

Q13 successor admission. `plans/gate_timing_check.py --lesson
    corpus/lessons/round-84.md --commit REV` must exit 0 in a scratch clone of
    the measured revision, using the checker bytes at REV. Exit 0 is q13=0.
    Any other exit, or an absent lesson, is q13=1. The checker itself requires a
    line-start "writer:" field on the candidate; that requirement is folded into
    q13 (the INFO line only observes it) so the frozen defect count stays three.

Counting: defects = q1 + q21 + q13 over entries=1. Exit 0 pass, 1 fail,
2 could-not-evaluate (entry absent at the revision, unreadable revision, or the
gate repository cannot be materialised). Could-not-evaluate prints one
COULD-NOT-EVALUATE line and no TARGET/PREDICATE line.

  --control-filler    BASE bytes, no repair: must stay defects=3.

The lane's own offline state check (`plans/state_check.py --summary`) compares frozen
self-assessment assertions against the repo.  At the round-85 tip exactly one assertion is
red: `P3c.box.4.pointer.1`, because `SHONEN.md` box 4 points at `PROVINCE.md:129` and the
instrument's pin freezes the same line, while `### Adjacent` moved to a later line as
PROVINCE.md grew.  This counter measures the repair, not the edit:

  P2-shonen    SHONEN.md box 4's first evidence pointer is `PROVINCE.md:<derived line>`
  P3-pin       the box-4 entry of `P3C_PINS` in plans/state_check.py carries the same
               derived line and the same token

               `VERDICT: PASS`, and exits 0
  P5-selftest  `plans/state_check.py --selftest` still exits 0 (the pin edit did not break
               the instrument that holds it)

A re-pin is legitimate only because P1 derives the number from bytes: restoring the stale
line (or hand-editing the pin without moving the pointer) fails P2 or P3 and leaves P4 red.
